_why: The citation ratchet, keyed by CONFIGURATION, because the checker does not measure the same
population in every configuration. With an ORCA checkout resolved, ~527 citations into ORCA's
tree are checked and ~129 paths are external; without one, those same paths fall to external
and the count is drawn from a partly DISJOINT set. A single number enforced across both is not
a threshold on anything: seven repairs moved the ORCA-resolved count 92 -> 85 and the
ORCA-absent count 98 -> 98, on the same pinned tree.
A number here is a RATCHET, not an amnesty. It may only go DOWN. Raising it to make a job
green is how a checker becomes decoration (PITFALLS P33). THE NUMBERS BELOW ARE NOT MET AT
HEAD AND HAVE DELIBERATELY NOT BEEN RAISED TO MEET IT — see `standing` vs `measured`.
Every reading was taken on a CLEAN DETACHED WORKTREE at the stated commit, with node_modules
symlinked in. A count taken in the shared working tree is not comparable: it reads whatever
five peers have uncommitted. The same tree read 139 while one peer had os-synth/index.ts open.

orca:87097551f8.why: Standing ratchet, measured clean at 98309f8. All 85 were in the three record documents - 006-fma 66, 014-review-round7 13, 008-crossreview-round3 6 - with zero live.

orca:absent.why: The CI configuration: GitHub's runner has no ORCA checkout. The same 85 plus 13 that only resolve in this configuration - five in 011-settings, two in 016, one in 002 pointing at another document, and four more in 006 the ORCA-resolved run classifies differently.

why: NOT MET, and not raised. The standing 85/98 were measured at 98309f8; commit 4ccfa20
(fix(os-synth): a reply beginning with `---` lost half of it) moved the ORCA-resolved total
from 85 to 130 in one commit, with no documentation changing at all. Bisected in a pinned
worktree with the instrument held fixed; a control run confirmed the checker change itself
moved the count by zero (85 with the old script and 85 with the new one at 98309f8).
So the gate is red for CODE CHURN in a heavily-cited file, and it has no honest path to
green: raising the number is decoration, and re-pointing the citations is HARMFUL for the
66 in 006-fma, which is stale by REMEDY rather than drift - its TT1 and TT2 rows describe
bare catches that have since been fixed, so a re-pointed citation would sit green beside a
sentence describing a defect that no longer exists.
A gate with no honest path to green is the finding, not the number. See
docs/.research/citation-audit.md, `What the ratchet should measure instead`.
